findings.title: False general-drift weighted Lipschitz extension used for the vanishing-viscosity gradient estimate

anchors: Proposition 8.1 (8.4) and its direct invocation of Lemma 4.3

all_operative_hypotheses: d=1, N>=2, sigma=1, beta=0
Smooth bounded drift b satisfying (4.2) with N-independent one-sided constant
Bounded smooth terminal g and source f satisfying weighted Lipschitz (4.3)
Classical bounded solutions on a fixed sufficiently short interval; constants claimed independent of N

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Set i=1, b=(a sin(x2),0,...,0), a>0, f=0, g=sin(x1). The symmetric Jacobian of b has eigenvalues +/-a cos(x2)/2, so (4.2) holds with M=a/2. In forward time s=T-t let v solve v_s-Delta v+(v_x1)^2/2+a sin(x2)v_x1=0, v(0)=sin(x1). A fixed short-time smooth periodic solution exists by heat-semigroup contraction and parabolic smoothing in two variables, independent of N. At the origin partial_s partial_x2 v(0,0)=-a; hence partial_x2 v(s*,0) is nonzero for some fixed small s*>0. The claimed weighted bound implies its absolute value <=c1/sqrt(N), impossible. The same initial jet refutes the linear transport variant. The original proof uses the special equality D_i u^i(x)=D_i u^i(y) at the doubling maximum to cancel its own drift; arbitrary b has no such cancellation.

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Original game-specific Lemma 4.3 is not refuted.
If D[u] is additionally retained as a hypothesis, the two-variable smooth example embedded with other components zero has an N-independent lower symmetric-Jacobian bound as well.
The arbitrary drift counterexample is not represented as the actual Nash drift in Proposition 8.1. Its extra structure might support a different estimate.
findings.core_dependency: Remark 4.4 general transport assertion -> direct componentwise application in Proposition 8.1 -> sigma-uniform gradient compactness in Theorem 3.17.
findings.repair: Supply a genuine game-specific weighted gradient estimate, or prove an appropriate weighted one-sided bound for the actual drift. Merely checking the forcing term (4.3), as on p69, is insufficient. No full replacement proof is certified.
findings.impact_boundary: False auxiliary extension and invalid core invocation established. No counterexample to Proposition 8.1 or Theorem 3.17 under corrected intended D-semimonotonicity is asserted.

independent_verification.source_claim: Remark 4.4 p30; componentwise invocation of Lemma 4.3 for (8.4), p69; compactness dependency p70.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: Read (4.2), (4.3), the stated constant dependence, and the full doubling argument pp25,27-30. Remark 4.4 sums the arbitrary drift over ALL j, so b1=a sin(x2) is actually included. Smooth bounded periodic two-variable data and a fixed short interval embed into every N>=2.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Re-derived the initial time equation and differentiated in x2: partial_s partial_x2 v(0,0)=-a. Smooth local existence follows from the two-dimensional heat-semigroup contraction with integrable time^-1/2 gradient kernel; it supplies a nonzero derivative at a fixed small time independent of N. The symmetric drift Jacobian has eigenvalues +/-a cos(x2)/2. Even retaining D[u], only a fixed two-dimensional block occurs, hence an N-independent lower bound exists. The claimed weighted estimate forces that nonzero derivative <=c1/sqrt(N), a contradiction.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The Nash-specific own-derivative equality at the doubling maximum is present in (4.6)-(4.10) and is absent for arbitrary b. The constructed drift is not asserted to be the actual Nash drift for Proposition 8.1. However, p69 checks only the forcing condition before the direct componentwise invocation; a game-specific gradient proof or an appropriate weighted drift estimate is still required.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Major confirmed for an invalid core invocation used to obtain sigma-uniform gradient compactness. Neither the original Nash value-function lemma nor the intended final theorem is claimed false by this arbitrary-drift example.

findings.title: The displayed assumption (3.9) admits a nonsmooth inviscid limit
all_operative_hypotheses: d=1, quadratic H=p^2/2, beta=0, T=2
F and G satisfy all regularity requirements of Remark 3.15
Printed (3.9) for F and G with arbitrarily small semimonotonicity constants
sigma_N>0 tends to zero and liminf sigma_N log log N can be infinite
Smooth bounded finite-N Nash solutions

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Choose F=0 and G(x,m)=cos(x), independent of m. All measure derivatives vanish; all spatial derivatives are bounded. Printed (3.9) uses x_i in both terms, so its left side is identically zero. Choose sigma_N=(log log N)^(-1/2) for sufficiently large N. The uncoupled Cole-Hopf solutions converge to V(s,x)=min_y{cos(y)+(x-y)^2/(2s)}, s=T-t. This limit follows directly from the positive heat integral and Laplace upper/lower bounds, since the quadratic term confines all minimizers. At s=2,x=0, the objective cos(y)+y^2/4 has exactly two minimizers +/-a, where a in (0,pi) solves a=2sin(a): y=0 is a strict local maximum, sin(y)/y is strictly decreasing on (0,pi), and outside [-pi,pi] the objective is greater than 1. The one-sided spatial slopes are +/-a/2, with a approximately 1.895494267033981. Thus the value limit is not differentiable at zero, whereas (3.11) and Theorem 3.17 require a bounded Lipschitz derivative.

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The text calls (3.9) D-semimonotonicity, strongly suggesting the second x_i should be y_i.
Under that intended replacement G'' has lower bound -1; the small D-semimonotonicity condition for T=2 excludes this example.
Section 8 invokes actual D-semimonotonicity from Proposition 5.1, which supports the intended interpretation.
findings.core_dependency: Displayed theorem hypothesis -> applicability of the D-semimonotonicity bootstrap -> claimed C1 inviscid subsequential limit.
findings.repair: Replace D_x F(x_i,m_y^-i) by D_x F(y_i,m_y^-i), likewise for G, and state explicitly that the smallness concerns Definition 3.1. This removes this counterexample but does not resolve P001.
findings.impact_boundary: Literal statement using displayed (3.9) is false. The theorem interpreted with the intended corrected D-semimonotonicity is not disproved.

independent_verification.source_claim: Repeated own-state argument in (3.9), p23, explicitly invoked by Theorem 3.17 p24.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: G(x,m)=cos(x), F=0 satisfy all bounded smooth regularity and measure conditions in Remark 3.15. Literal (3.9) is identically zero for measure-independent data. For large N, sigma_N=(log log N)^(-1/2) has the required zero limit and infinite scaled liminf.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Verified the Cole-Hopf transform signs for v_s-sigma v_xx+v_x^2/2=0. Laplace bounds on the positive Gaussian integral yield the value limit without assuming derivative convergence. At s=2,x=0 the objective cos(y)+y^2/4 has a local maximum at zero, exactly one positive critical minimum solving sin(a)/a=1/2, and no global minima outside [-pi,pi] since -1+pi^2/4>1. The two minima +/-a give left/right slopes +a/2 and -a/2. Thus even the value limit at a fixed empirical measure cannot have the claimed derivative.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Definition 3.1 uses the full own-state difference. Replacing the second x^i by y^i requires G semimonotonicity constant at least 1; Proposition 5.1 p40 supplies Mg_star=(12eT)^(-1)<1 at T=2. The intended smallness regime excludes this example. The report correctly distinguishes that intended theorem from its literal displayed hypothesis.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Major confirmed for a literal principal-theorem hypothesis admitting a nonsmooth limit, with the intended-reading limitation retained. This does not repair the separate P001 gap.

findings.title: Incorrect label normalization and omitted terminal gradient term in Lemma 7.1
all_operative_hypotheses: d=1, sigma=1, beta=0, H=p^2/2, fixed T>0
Smooth bounded f,g satisfying MF, S, LP and LS with constants independent of N
Large N, labels in [0,1], ordinary Euclidean norm as defined
Classical Nash solutions with (7.1a)-(7.1b)

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Let f_i=0 and g_i=lambda_i sin(x_i)+epsilon/(N-1) sum_{j!=i}sin(x_j), 0<epsilon<=1. All hypotheses hold: smoothness and uniform bounds, own-label symmetry, LP, MF (take Lg=2), and L[g]=0 by separability. Define v_lambda(s,x)=-2 log E exp[-lambda sin(x+sqrt(2)B_s)/2] and w_lambda=partial_lambda v_lambda. Since v_s=v_xx-v_x^2/2 and w_s=w_xx-v_x w_x, the exact Nash solution is u_i=v_lambda_i(s,x_i)+epsilon/(N-1)sum_{j!=i}w_lambda_j(s,x_j). Take lambda_1=lambda'_1=0, all other labels 1 versus 0, and all x=0. The value difference is epsilon|w_1(s,0)|>0 independent of N; symmetry yields E[S exp(-S/2)]=-E[S sinh(S/2)]<0 for S=sin(sqrt(2)B_s). The asserted bound C sqrt(N-1)/N tends to zero. At s=1, epsilon=1/4, reviewer quadrature gives about 0.05956859624. Independently, (7.3) at tau=T forces D_i(g_lambda_i-g_lambda'_i)=0, contradicted by lambda_i sin(x_i).

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The counting in the proof is an l1 sum; if its norm notation were redefined as l1, the scaling objection would disappear, but p13 explicitly uses Euclidean norm.
The correct l1/N or l2/sqrt(N) size remains compatible with Wasserstein compactness.
No counterexample to Theorem 7.5 itself is given.
findings.core_dependency: Label stability -> Remark 7.2 single-label derivative control -> compactness and label dependence of the heterogeneous limit.
findings.repair: Use C(|Delta lambda_1|+N^-1 sum_{j>1}|Delta lambda_j|), or its l2/sqrt(N) consequence. Restore the terminal derivative contribution in the short-interval estimate and justify the componentwise gradient estimate before iteration. A complete replacement gradient proof is not claimed.
findings.impact_boundary: The written uniform label estimate is false, including for exact bounded Nash solutions. Required normalization and missing terminal data are identified; intended compactness conclusion is not disproved.

independent_verification.source_claim: Lemma 7.1 p51 and terminal-term-free (7.3) p52, under Euclidean norm convention p13.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: Checked MF p17, LS p14/18, S/LP p20 and the Section 7 bounds. The proposed additive sine terminal data are bounded uniformly in N, symmetric in other states, Lipschitz in own label, and have zero rectangular LS expression. Lg=2 controls all the displayed MF rows for N>=2.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Differentiated the scalar Cole-Hopf equation in lambda, obtaining w_s=w_xx-v_x w_x. Substituting the sum of v_lambda_i and epsilon/(N-1) w_lambda_j into the Nash system cancels every other-player transport term and gives exactly the stated terminal data. With own label zero, opposite choices of all other labels give epsilon|w1(s,0)| independent of N. Symmetry yields the strictly negative numerator -E[S sinh(S/2)], while the claimed Euclidean bound is C sqrt(N-1)/N. At tau=T, (7.3) also contradicts a nonzero terminal own gradient.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The summation needs l1/N, implying l2/sqrt(N), and the terminal derivative must be retained. These scales permit the intended Wasserstein compactness and the single-label N^-1 estimate; the report explicitly leaves a complete componentwise gradient replacement unproved.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained for the demonstrated normalization/terminal-data errors within the stated repair boundary, without alleging the heterogeneous limit theorem false.

findings.title: Missing label distance and opposite cross-diffusion sign in Lemma 7.13

anchors: Coupling PDE and derivative of quadratic coupling cost

all_operative_hypotheses: Bounded drift B, globally Lipschitz in label, state and joint measure uniformly in time
Lambda=[0,1], P2 initial joint laws and their disintegrations
All pairs lambda,lambda' in the displayed conditional estimate

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Take B^lambda=lambda, rho uniform on [0,1], mu_0=rho tensor delta_0 and tilde mu=mu. Each conditional law at time t is Normal(lambda t,2t), so W2=t|lambda-lambda'|, while every initial and global distance on the right of (7.25) vanishes. Separately, the printed coupling PDE has +2 partial_xy on its left. For B=0 and initial delta_(0,0), it is solved by (X,Y)=(sqrt(2)W,-sqrt(2)W), and E|X-Y|^2=8t, contradicting the displayed no-diffusion derivative identity. Synchronous noise requires the cross term -2 partial_xy.

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The same-label case and the joint-law estimate (7.24) are not refuted.
The intended synchronous coupling and a label-distance term give the usual Gronwall estimate under the written Lipschitz assumption.
findings.core_dependency: Coupling estimate -> continuity/stability of disintegrated flows -> Lemma 7.14 and Theorem 7.11.
findings.repair: Add C|lambda-lambda'| to (7.25), propagate it through the drift comparison, and reverse the mixed diffusion sign. Direct synchronous stochastic coupling proves the corrected estimate.
findings.impact_boundary: False quantitative conditional statement and coupling identity; no failure of the intended McKean-Vlasov well-posedness conclusion established.

independent_verification.source_claim: All-label (7.25) and mixed-diffusion PDE p60; zero-noise-cost differentiation p61.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: B(lambda,x,mu)=lambda is bounded and globally Lipschitz on Lambda=[0,1], with identical global initial laws and a continuous choice of all initial conditionals delta_0. The statement really quantifies over lambda and lambda_prime separately.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: The Fokker-Planck sign in (7.23) gives Normal(lambda*t,2t). Equal covariance implies W2=t|lambda-lambda_prime|, while both initial distances on the printed right side vanish. For zero drift the printed mixed sign gives generator partial_xx+partial_yy-2partial_xy, whose action on (x-y)^2 is 8, so the claimed cancellation is impossible.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: With synchronous noise the left mixed sign is negative. Subtracting the coupled SDEs gives a drift difference bounded by L(|lambda-lambda_prime|+|X-Y|+W2(mu,mutilde)); Gronwall supplies the missing label term. Same-label and joint-law stability remain compatible.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained because these explicit local changes recover the coupling estimate under the written Lipschitz hypotheses, without a well-posedness counterexample.

findings.title: Label-mass transfer is absent from the empirical-measure bound
all_operative_hypotheses: Finite populations with positive fixed weights theta summing to one
Partition counts a_k=#I_k^N/N tend to theta_k; no rate required
Initial laws with q>4 moments and bounded drifts; joint label-state W2 metric

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Choose two labels 0 and 1, weights (1/2,1/2), all initial positions zero, zero costs/drift, and an alternating partition. For any odd N, the weights differ by 1/(2N); W2 squared between the two joint atomic laws equals 1/(2N)>0. The displayed bound 2 max_i|X_i|^2 sum_k|a_k-theta_k| is zero. This satisfies the initial and moment assumptions at t=0; N can be arbitrarily large. Bounded drift also does not give a uniform second-moment bound for the maximum over independent Brownian particles. A correct common-mass coupling, writing eta_k=delta_lambda_k tensor nu_k, gives W2^2(sum a_k eta_k,sum theta_k eta_k)<=2 sum |a_k-theta_k| int(1+|x|^2)nu_k(dx). Retain min(a_k,theta_k) on the diagonal and couple only the remaining equal masses; the label cost is at most one and |x-y|^2<=2|x|^2+2|y|^2. Group-average moment bounds then imply convergence without a count-rate assumption.

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The actual periodic partitions used later have an O(1/N) discrepancy, which is stronger than Lemma 7.15 assumes.
The corrected average-moment coupling suffices for the stated finite-population convergence mechanism.
The located publisher correction concerns footnote marker 7 rather than this inequality.
findings.core_dependency: Joint empirical-law comparison -> gamma_N error -> (7.34) Gronwall estimate -> finite-population representation.
findings.repair: Replace the maximum-position bound by the proved common-mass average-moment bound, including label distance. Use bounded-drift individual/group average moments to pass to expectation.
findings.impact_boundary: Displayed estimate is false even at the initial time. A local replacement bound is proved; the lemma's convergence conclusion is not refuted.

independent_verification.source_claim: Joint empirical-law weight bound after (7.32), p64; natural-density assumptions pp62-63.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: Two labels 0 and 1, zero data/drift, zero initial states, and an alternating partition satisfy all moment and finite-population assumptions, for arbitrarily large odd N. The metric includes the label coordinate.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: The excess atom mass is 1/(2N), which must move unit label distance, so W2^2=1/(2N)>0 while the printed position-only bound is zero. Independently derived the repair: keep common masses min(a_k,theta_k); if delta is the remaining mass, couple excess and deficit by their normalized product. Label cost <=delta and state cost <=2 sum |a_k-theta_k| int |x|^2 dnu_k, which is bounded by the report displayed formula.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Bounded drift and finite initial second moments give a uniform bound on each E sup_t |X_i|^2 and hence each group average, not a uniform particle maximum. Since the number of groups is fixed and the count discrepancies tend to zero, the replacement tends to zero in expectation without any rate assumption. Later periodic partitions have stronger rates but are not needed for this repair.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained for a false error bound with a proved replacement sufficient for its Gronwall use. The retained publisher notice concerns footnote-marker placement, not this inequality.

findings.title: Nonsymmetric matrix order does not imply the claimed vanishing or norm equivalence
all_operative_hypotheses: Matrix positivity is the quadratic-form convention even for nonsymmetric matrices
Remark 3.4 assumes C2 L-monotone data, without symmetry of the mixed Jacobian
Section 9 invokes MF and N-independent gradient-map Lipschitz constants

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: For N=2,d=1, take h1=sin(x1)sin(x2), h2=-sin(x1)sin(x2). The four-point L expression cancels identically, but the zero-diagonal mixed matrix is [[0,c],[-c,0]], c=cos(x1)cos(x2), and h1 has nonzero mixed derivative; it is not own-state-plus-other-state separable. Also K=[[0,1],[-1,0]] has zero quadratic form and operator norm one, disproving equivalence of a two-sided quadratic-form bound and an operator-norm bound after (9.8). Finally gi=sin(x_i) satisfies MF with Lg=2 independently of N, whereas sum_ij ||D_ji gi||_infinity^2=N, contradicting the asserted <=2Lg^2 for N>8. Its actual operator norm is one.

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Only the symmetric part must vanish in the first example.
The forward implication from the genuine Lipschitz bound (9.8) to quadratic-form control is valid and is sufficient for that drift comparison.
An N-independent operator bound follows by splitting diagonal and off-diagonal blocks; thus the Frobenius overestimate need not damage the intended theorem.
findings.core_dependency: Structural discussion of L-monotonicity and the initial operator estimate used to propagate general-Hamiltonian one-sided drift bounds.
findings.repair: Conclude only that the symmetric off-diagonal part vanishes; drop the false reverse equivalence. Bound the diagonal part in operator norm and the off-diagonal part by its Frobenius norm: ||J||op<=2Lg, giving Cg^2<=4Lg^2 (and similarly for f).
findings.impact_boundary: Three explicit auxiliary linear-algebra implications fail; corrected bounds preserve the needed N independence. No general-Hamiltonian final theorem is disproved.

independent_verification.source_claim: Remark 3.4 p15, reverse equivalence after (9.8) p75, full-Frobenius estimate p76.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: Source p11 explicitly permits nonsymmetric matrices in quadratic-form order; p13 distinguishes Euclidean/Frobenius norms. No symmetry of the mixed Jacobian is imposed.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Expanded both rectangular differences of +/-sin(x1)sin(x2); they cancel identically, while the mixed derivative at zero is 1 and the matrix is skew. For K=[[0,1],[-1,0]], xi^T K xi=0 and K^T K=I, disproving the reverse norm equivalence. For g_i=sin(x_i), MF holds with Lg=2 but the sum of squared Hessian entries is N, exceeding 8 for N>8.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Only the symmetric off-diagonal part is forced to vanish. Genuine operator control implies the quadratic-form bound in the direction needed. Summing the MF off-diagonal row bounds gives Frobenius norm <=Lg; the diagonal operator norm is <=Lg, so total operator norm <=2Lg and Cg^2<=4Lg^2 independently of N.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained for three auxiliary implications with explicit corrections preserving the dimension independence needed by the following comparison.

findings.title: Incorrect representation signs and constants in Appendix A

anchors: Theorem A.1 heat kernel and Duhamel formula
(A.2), associated forward equation and final sup norm bound

all_operative_hypotheses: Smooth bounded f,g satisfying MF and either DS-H1 or LS-H1prime with sufficiently small constants and large N
H bounded below, smooth on bounded p sets and satisfying H0; sigma>0,beta>=0
Continuation argument uses a uniform value bound in addition to derivative bounds

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Take d=1, sigma=1, beta=0, H=c+p^2/2 with c>0, f=g=0, any sufficiently large N. All smoothness, MF, DS/LS and convexity assumptions hold. The exact bounded solution is ui(t,x)=c(t-T). Formula (A.2) instead gives c(T-t), and the final displayed supremum bound on p82 is zero. Along drift -D_p H the correct integrand is f-H+D_p H dot p, and the forward equation has minus divergence of D_p H rho. Convexity yields the lower estimate f-H(x,0). In Step 1, J=J_N tensor I_d has eigenvalue N of multiplicity d: det(sigma I+beta J)=sigma^(Nd)(1+N beta/sigma)^d and inverse=sigma^-1(I-beta J/(sigma+N beta)). The printed Nd substitution is wrong for d>1; N=1,d=2,sigma=beta=1 gives determinant 4 instead of 3. The time integral must use Phi(s-t)*(f-w(s)), whereas w(s-t) can be outside its time domain.

alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: The constant-shift example is an exact existing solution, so it does not refute existence or uniqueness.
The invariant matrix form of the heat kernel printed before its scalar expansion is correct.
A corrected value bound may depend on the positive part of H(x,0), as allowed by fixed-H constants.
findings.core_dependency: Local heat fixed point and stochastic representation -> uniform C_b^1 continuation bound (A.1) -> Theorem A.1.
findings.repair: Correct the forward drift and running-cost signs; include ||H(.,0)^+||infinity as well as the negative lower bound of H in the value estimate. Use the matrix kernel or its correct eigenvalue expansion and correct Duhamel times. These are local formula repairs, not a replacement proof of all external Schauder inputs.
findings.impact_boundary: Printed representation and value bound are false under the theorem's assumptions. The continuation theorem itself is not refuted.

independent_verification.source_claim: Appendix A pp79-82: scalar kernel expansion, Duhamel times, (A.2), forward drift sign and final supremum bound.
independent_verification.hypothesis_check: H=c+p^2/2, c>0, f=g=0 meets H0, both convexity alternatives, all smoothness and zero semimonotonicity assumptions, with arbitrarily large N. No H(x,0)=0 normalization is required.
independent_verification.independent_proof_check: Substituted u=c(t-T) into the PDE: residual zero; the printed integral gives its opposite and the asserted absolute-value bound gives zero. Applying Ito along drift -DpH yields running cost f-H+DpH dot p; convexity bounds this below by f-H(x,0). Diagonalizing J_N tensor I_d gives eigenvalue N of multiplicity d and zero of multiplicity (N-1)d, establishing the report determinant/inverse. For d=2,sigma=beta=1 the determinant discrepancy persists for every N, including arbitrarily large N: (1+N)^2 versus 1+2N. The backward Duhamel semigroup is Phi(s-t) applied to f-w(s), not the printed time arguments.

Restoring the running-cost/forward signs, correct kernel/time arguments and positive H(.,0) dependence supplies the local formulas and value bound used for continuation. The constant-shift example itself is a bounded regular solution; existence/uniqueness and all external Schauder inputs are not claimed disproved or independently reproved.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Minor retained for explicit representation/value-estimate errors with the stated local repair scope.

findings.title: Compactness lemma lacks a separability condition on the parameter space
all_operative_hypotheses: Gamma is declared to be an arbitrary metric space
Finite-dimensional normed E; h_N bounded and symmetric on E^N
Uniform concave moduli in Gamma and empirical Wp, p>=1
One common subsequence asserted to converge on every compact H and K

decisive_evidence.type: Self-contained analytic counterexample or exact derivation; independent symbolic/numerical corroboration
decisive_evidence.proof: Take Gamma={0,1}^{natural numbers} with the discrete metric, E=R, and h_N(gamma,v)=gamma_N. Choose C=1 and both moduli omega(r)=r. All hypotheses hold; the empirical variable is irrelevant. For any subsequence N_k choose a single gamma with gamma_{N_k}=k modulo 2. This is an infinite diagonal argument, not a finite numerical demonstration.
